quests.hint: The first meal of the day - eaten in the morning after waking up.
quests.explanation: 'Breakfast' is the first meal of the day. It provides energy for the morning and is often called the most important meal.
quests.definition: The first meal of the day, eaten in the morning.
quests.example: I always eat a healthy breakfast of eggs and toast before going to work.
quests.usageExample: The word "BREAKFAST" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: The midday meal - eaten around noon.
quests.explanation: 'Lunch' is the meal eaten in the middle of the day, usually between noon and 2 p.m.
quests.definition: The meal eaten in the middle of the day, around noon.
quests.example: We usually have a one-hour break for lunch at the office.
quests.usageExample: The word "LUNCH" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: The evening meal - the main meal of the day for most families.
quests.explanation: 'Dinner' is the main meal of the day, usually eaten in the evening. Families often eat dinner together.
quests.definition: The main meal of the day, typically eaten in the evening.
quests.example: We had a wonderful three-course dinner at the new Italian restaurant downtown.
quests.usageExample: The word "DINNER" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: A hot brown drink made from roasted beans - many people drink it in the morning.
quests.explanation: 'Coffee' is a popular hot drink made from roasted coffee beans. It contains caffeine, which helps people feel alert.
quests.definition: A popular hot drink made from roasted and ground coffee beans.
quests.example: Would you like a cup of coffee with milk and sugar?
quests.usageExample: The word "COFFEE" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: A classic British afternoon drink, often served with milk.
quests.explanation: 'Tea' is a hot drink made by pouring boiling water over tea leaves. It is the most popular drink in many countries.
quests.definition: A hot drink made by pouring boiling water over dried tea leaves.
quests.example: She drinks green tea every morning because it is good for her health.
quests.usageExample: The word "TEA" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: A basic food staple made from flour and water, often in a loaf.
quests.explanation: 'Bread' is a staple food made from flour, water, and yeast baked in an oven. It is eaten worldwide every day.
quests.definition: A staple food made from flour and water, baked in an oven.
quests.example: I buy fresh bread from the bakery every Sunday morning.
quests.usageExample: The word "BREAD" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: Oranges, apples, bananas, and grapes are all examples of this.
quests.explanation: 'Fruit' is the sweet or sour product of a plant that contains seeds. Eating fruit is important for a healthy diet.
quests.definition: The sweet or sour part of a plant that contains seeds and is eaten as food.
quests.example: Doctors recommend eating at least two portions of fruit every day.
quests.usageExample: The word "FRUIT" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: Carrots, broccoli, potatoes, and onions are examples of this.
quests.explanation: 'Vegetable' is a plant or part of a plant eaten as food. Vegetables provide essential vitamins and minerals.
quests.definition: A plant or part of a plant that is eaten as food, providing vitamins and minerals.
quests.example: She tries to eat at least five different vegetables every day.
quests.usageExample: The word "VEGETABLE" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: A white grain staple food popular in Asia - cooked in water.
quests.explanation: 'Rice' is a grain grown in flooded fields, especially in Asia. It is one of the world's most important food staples.
quests.definition: A white or brown grain cooked and eaten as a staple food worldwide.
quests.example: We had chicken curry served with steamed white rice for dinner.
quests.usageExample: The word "RICE" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: A popular meat from a bird - often roasted or fried.
quests.explanation: 'Chicken' is poultry (a type of bird) that is widely eaten as food. It is one of the world's most popular sources of protein.
quests.definition: A common domesticated bird whose meat is widely eaten as food.
quests.example: She made a delicious roast chicken with herbs and garlic for Sunday lunch.
quests.usageExample: The word "CHICKEN" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: The conditions outside - is it raining, sunny, cold, or windy?
quests.explanation: 'Weather' describes the atmospheric conditions at a particular time and place, including temperature, rainfall, and wind.
quests.definition: The atmospheric conditions outside, including temperature, rain, and wind.
quests.example: The weather forecast says it will rain heavily this afternoon.
quests.usageExample: The word "WEATHER" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: Water falling from clouds in the sky - you need an umbrella for this.
quests.explanation: 'Rain' is water that falls from clouds. Rain is essential for plants and fills rivers and reservoirs.
quests.definition: Water that falls from clouds in drops.
quests.example: It rained so heavily last night that the streets were flooded this morning.
quests.usageExample: The word "RAIN" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: The bright star at the centre of our solar system - it gives us light and warmth.
quests.explanation: 'Sun' is the star at the centre of our solar system. It provides the light and heat that make life on Earth possible.
quests.definition: The star at the centre of our solar system that provides light and heat.
quests.example: The sun was shining brightly so we spent the afternoon at the beach.
quests.usageExample: The word "SUN" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: Moving air that you can feel on your face outdoors.
quests.explanation: 'Wind' is moving air. A gentle wind is called a breeze, and a very strong wind is called a storm or gale.
quests.definition: Moving air, especially strong moving air felt outdoors.
quests.example: The wind was so strong yesterday that it blew leaves off all the trees.
quests.usageExample: The word "WIND" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: Frozen white crystals that fall from the sky in winter.
quests.explanation: 'Snow' is precipitation that forms as white ice crystals and falls from clouds in cold weather.
quests.definition: Frozen water that falls from the sky as white flakes in cold weather.
quests.example: The children were very excited when they woke up to find snow covering the garden.
quests.usageExample: The word "SNOW" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: One of the four divisions of the year - spring, summer, autumn, winter.
quests.explanation: 'Season' is one of the four divisions of the year. Each season has different weather and daylight patterns.
quests.definition: One of the four natural divisions of the year with different weather conditions.
quests.example: Autumn is my favourite season because I love the colours of the falling leaves.
quests.usageExample: The word "SEASON" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: The season after winter when flowers bloom and trees grow new leaves.
quests.explanation: 'Spring' is the season between winter and summer. Temperatures rise, flowers bloom, and days become longer.
quests.definition: The season between winter and summer when plants begin to grow and flowers bloom.
quests.example: In spring, the park is full of colourful tulips and blossoming cherry trees.
quests.usageExample: The word "SPRING" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: The hottest season - people go to beaches and on holiday.
quests.explanation: 'Summer' is the hottest season of the year. Schools are often on holiday in summer, and people go to the beach.
quests.definition: The warmest season of the year, coming after spring.
quests.example: We spent the whole summer at the lake house swimming and relaxing.
quests.usageExample: The word "SUMMER" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: The cool season when leaves change colour and fall from trees.
quests.explanation: 'Autumn' (called 'fall' in American English) is the season between summer and winter when leaves change colour.
quests.definition: The season between summer and winter when leaves change colour and fall.
quests.example: We go apple picking every autumn at the farm near our village.
quests.usageExample: The word "AUTUMN" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: The coldest season - there may be snow and short days.
quests.explanation: 'Winter' is the coldest season of the year. In winter, days are short, temperatures are low, and there may be snow.
quests.definition: The coldest season of the year with short days and low temperatures.
quests.example: We stayed indoors by the fire all winter because it was bitterly cold outside.
quests.usageExample: The word "WINTER" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: Not warm - the temperature is moderate, not hot or cold.
quests.explanation: 'Cool' describes a temperature that is pleasantly low but not cold. A cool breeze on a summer day is refreshing.
quests.definition: At a pleasantly low temperature; not warm or cold.
quests.example: The evening air was cool and refreshing after a very hot summer's day.
quests.usageExample: The word "COOL" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: A pleasant temperature - not cold, comfortable for being outside.
quests.explanation: 'Warm' describes a moderately high and comfortable temperature. A warm day is perfect for outdoor activities.
quests.definition: Having a moderately high and comfortable temperature; not hot or cold.
quests.example: It was a warm sunny afternoon, perfect for having a picnic in the park.
quests.usageExample: The word "WARM" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: How hot or cold something is - measured in degrees.
quests.explanation: 'Temperature' is a measure of how hot or cold something is. Body temperature, weather, and cooking all involve temperature.
quests.definition: A measure of how hot or cold something is, measured in degrees.
quests.example: The temperature dropped to minus five degrees last night, which was very unusual.
quests.usageExample: The word "TEMPERATURE" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: When the sky is covered with clouds and little sunlight gets through.
quests.explanation: 'Cloudy' describes weather when the sky is covered by clouds. A cloudy day may mean rain is coming.
quests.definition: Having a sky that is mostly covered with clouds; overcast.
quests.example: It was cloudy all morning but the sun finally came out in the afternoon.
quests.usageExample: The word "CLOUDY" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: When the sun is shining brightly - not cloudy or rainy.
quests.explanation: 'Sunny' describes weather when the sun is shining brightly in a clear sky. Sunny days are great for outdoor activities.
quests.definition: Bright with sunlight; having clear, sunny weather.
quests.example: Let's have a barbecue in the garden — it's going to be sunny all weekend.
quests.usageExample: The word "SUNNY" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: How you feel when you have not eaten for a long time.
quests.explanation: 'Hungry' describes the uncomfortable feeling of needing food. We feel hungry when our body needs energy from food.
quests.definition: Feeling the need to eat because you have not had food for a while.
quests.example: I was so hungry after the long hike that I ate three sandwiches.
quests.usageExample: The word "HUNGRY" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: How you feel when you need a drink of water.
quests.explanation: 'Thirsty' describes the feeling of needing a drink. We become thirsty when our body needs water.
quests.definition: Feeling the need to drink because your body needs water.
quests.example: After playing football for an hour, he was extremely thirsty.
quests.usageExample: The word "THIRSTY" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You feel this when you have worked a lot and need rest.
quests.explanation: 'Tired' describes the feeling of needing sleep or rest after activity or effort. A good night's sleep cures tiredness.
quests.definition: Feeling a need for rest or sleep after activity or effort.
quests.example: She was so tired after the long journey that she fell asleep immediately.
quests.usageExample: The word "TIRED" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You feel this at parties or before doing something new and exciting.
quests.explanation: 'Excited' describes a feeling of enthusiasm and eagerness. People feel excited before good events and opportunities.
quests.definition: Feeling enthusiasm and eagerness about something enjoyable or interesting.
quests.example: The children were so excited on Christmas Eve that they could not sleep.
quests.usageExample: The word "EXCITED" can be used in many situations.

quests.hint: You feel this before an exam or doing something scary for the first time.
quests.explanation: 'Nervous' describes a feeling of anxiety or worry, especially before something important like an exam or interview.
quests.definition: Feeling anxious or worried, especially before an important or challenging event.
quests.example: She was very nervous before her first job interview but it went very well.
quests.usageExample: The word "NERVOUS" can be used in many situations.
